All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [0.29.0] - 2026-10-22

### Added

* **Agent Card A2A de un agente en Nexus (Nexus 0.27.0+).** El editor de un agente de Nexus suma el botón «A2A»: un panel que trae la card que Nexus sirve para ese agente (con la credencial del tenant y `A2A-Version: 1.0`) y muestra la URL de la card para copiar, el endpoint JSON-RPC, la versión viva, la descripción, las skills y si anuncia streaming y push. Distingue un agente no publicado (falta `spec.a2a.publicar: true` en la versión viva) de un Nexus que no sirve A2A (anterior a 0.27 o sin `NEXUS_PUBLIC_URL`), y avisa si la card no tiene descripción. Sólo lee: nunca corre el agente.

## [0.28.0] - 2026-10-21

### Added

* **Tools `type: a2a` (core 0.74.0).** El schema acepta un agente A2A remoto como tool, espejo de `build_a2a_tool`: `card_url` obligatoria (https salvo `policy.allow_insecure_http: true`, sin credenciales en la URL), `auth` con exactamente una de `api_key_env`/`bearer_env` (el nombre de la variable, nunca el secreto), `policy` (`max_bytes` 1 B–16 MiB, `timeout` (0, 600], `accept_parts` de `text`/`data`/`file`), `description` opcional, `rate_limit` y `max_result_tokens`; sin `parameters` ni `confirm`. El inspector de Tools ofrece «Agente A2A» con un formulario que valida como el core (hosts entre corchetes sólo IPv6, como `urlsplit`; U+0085; claves de `policy` desconocidas; `auth` vacío) y avisa que en el pool de Nexus sólo existen las variables que puso el operador. Una descripción vacía no escribe la clave, así el core la arma con la card.
* **Bloque A2A (core 0.73.0, Nexus 0.27.0).** Un bloque nuevo del editor visual edita `spec.a2a.publicar`, la descripción de la card (`spec.identity.description`) y `spec.skills` (`id`, `name`, `description`, `tags`), y marca las skills que el runtime omitiría (también un valor no string) y los ids repetidos. Agregar el bloque no publica (`publicar: false`); quitarlo borra las dos secciones. Los tags se separan al salir del campo, así se pueden escribir comas y espacios. El schema declara `spec.skills`, `spec.a2a` e `identity.name`.
* Snippets `tool-a2a`, `skills` y `a2a` en el autocompletado, y secciones Skills y A2A en el YamlHelper.

### Fixed

* **Snippets que insertaban YAML inválido.** El de `memory` escribía `backend`/`max_tokens` planos (el core no los lee y el schema los rechaza) y el de `permissions`, `allowed_tools`/`max_cost_per_request`; ahora insertan `memory.conversational` con redis y `allowed_actions`/`denied_actions`. El YamlHelper mostraba `permissions.filesystem`/`network`/`execution`, que el core descarta. Un test valida cada snippet de `spec` contra el schema.

### Changed

* Las fixtures de `config/agents` siguen idénticas a las de core 0.74.1.

## [0.27.0] - 2026-10-17

### Changed

* **Permissions, memoria semántica/episódica, swarm y `timeout_seconds` editables (paridad con core P1).** El schema y los inspectores ya no marcan estas secciones como inertes: `permissions.allowed_actions`/`denied_actions` (patrones fnmatch sobre las tools registradas, con sugerencias), `memory.semantic` (chromadb|faiss|pgvector|qdrant + `embeddings`, `dimension`, `path`, `connection.url`), `memory.episodic` (postgres), `orchestration.timeout_seconds` y `orchestration.max_handoffs`. `swarm` pide al menos una tool `type: agent`, como supervisor. Fixtures de core re-copiadas.
* **Agentes nuevos con `timeout_seconds: 120`.** El formulario de agente nuevo, el snippet de `orchestration` del YamlHelper y el de autocompletado (que además usaba el alias deprecado `timeout: 30`) ponían 30-60 s, que en core 0.71 cortan con 504 un modelo frío con una tool. El schema dice que la memoria semántica y episódica es de la sesión.

## [0.26.0] - 2026-10-16

### Added

* **`kind: Eval` (core 0.67.0).** Schema `eval.schema.json` para los `*.eval.yaml` de `astromesh-eval`, espejo de `astromesh/evals/formato.py`: `agent`, `thresholds.pass_rate`, `judge`, `tools_default`, `cases`/`cases_file` y asserts de una clave; además un caso necesita `expect` o `rubric`, una `rubric` necesita `judge` y hace falta al menos un caso. Monaco lo aplica a `*.eval.yaml` y ofrece el snippet `eval-skeleton`.
* **Corridas bloqueadas por guardrail en la consola local (core 0.70.0).** `blocked` y `guardrail {direction, rule, reason}` se leen por HTTP y del `done` del WebSocket; el mensaje muestra un chip con la regla en vez de parecer una respuesta normal.
* El inspector de modelo suma `context_window` por candidato y `centinela` como fuente, y sugiere los roles `summarizer` y `stage:<nombre>`.

### Fixed

* **El editor visual perdía claves del modelo al guardar.** `normalizeModelConfig` copiaba una lista blanca y borraba `context_window`, `max_retries` e `invalid_policy`, y reescribía `source: centinela`. Ahora pasa todas las claves del candidato.
* **Falsos errores en manifiestos que core acepta.** El schema de agente acepta la forma legacy `model.primary`/`fallback`/`extra`/`routing` (y `provider` como alias de `source`), `prompts.templates`, `orchestration.role_map` y `memory.conversational.connection.url`; `contract` de centinela es un objeto. Los 11 `config/agents/*.agent.yaml` de core validan limpio.
* El inspector de memoria escribía `memory.type` y `memory.max_history`, que core nunca leyó; ahora edita `memory.conversational` (`backend: redis`, `connection.url`, `strategy`, `max_turns`, `ttl`) y avisa cuando falta la url.
* El inspector de orquestación persistía `max_iterations: 10` y `timeout_seconds: 30` inventados; ahora un campo vacío es la clave ausente. `supervisor` ofrece elegir sus trabajadores y avisa que sin una tool `type: agent` el agente no carga.
* El schema de workflow acepta `parallel`, `when` y `strict_conditions`, exige exactamente un tipo de paso y rechaza el prefijo reservado `__chain__`.

### Changed

* Una tool `type: api` ya no acepta `confirm`: core sólo lo lee en `integration` y en `api` no gateaba nada.
* Los backends conversacionales distintos de `redis`, `permissions`, `timeout_seconds` y `swarm` se marcan como inertes en core 0.70.0.

## [0.25.0] - 2026-10-14

### Added

* **Paridad del schema con astromesh core 0.70.0 (guardrails).** `spec.guardrails` ahora se aplica en el core y el schema lo refleja: tipos `pii_detection`, `topic_filter`, `max_length`, `content_filter` y `cost_limit`, cada uno con sus acciones (la default primero), `message`, los alias `forbidden_topics` y `max_characters`, `blocked_patterns`, `forbidden_keywords` y `count`. `content_filter` sólo aplica en output, `topic_filter` y `max_length` sólo en input, y `cost_limit` exige `max_tokens_per_turn`.

### Changed

* El inspector visual de Guardrails editaba un mapa de nombres que el core nunca leyó; ahora edita la lista de reglas de input y output. Los snippets y la ayuda del editor YAML usan sólo lo que el core acepta.

### Removed

* `prompt_injection` y la acción `log` ya no se presentan como válidos: el core los descarta con un warning. `blocked_categories` y `allowed_topics` tampoco se soportan (necesitan un clasificador).

## [0.24.0] - 2026-10-11

### Added

* **Paridad del schema con astromesh core 0.68.0.** `spec.knowledge` acepta `bundle`, el directorio de un knowledge bundle Open Knowledge Format que el agente navega con `kb_index`, `kb_read` y `kb_find`, y exige `pipeline` o `bundle` (antes exigía `pipeline`). El inspector visual de Knowledge suma el campo OKF bundle.

## [0.23.0] - 2026-10-06

### Added

* **Paridad del schema con astromesh core 0.66.0.** El schema de agente acepta `max_result_tokens` (entero >= 1) en cada tool, de cualquier tipo, y `orchestration.max_tool_result_tokens` (entero >= 1), los topes de tokens del resultado de una tool (0.66.0). Acepta también `orchestration.stages` (2 a 6 nombres de 1 a 40 caracteres) del patrón `pipeline` (0.65.0), que el core ya leía y el schema rechazaba. Sin editor visual: se editan en el YAML.

## [0.22.0] - 2026-10-06

### Added

* **Paridad del schema con astromesh core 0.64.0.** El schema de agente acepta `spec.prompts.context` (template Jinja de lo que cambia por turno; el system prompt queda como prefijo cacheable) y `context_window` en cada candidato de modelo (fija el presupuesto del historial). Sin editor visual para estos campos: se editan en el YAML.

### Fixed

* **Candidatos `centinela`.** El schema rechazaba `source: centinela`, `max_retries` e `invalid_policy`, que el core ya aceptaba.

## [0.21.0](https://github.com/monaccode/astromesh-cortex/compare/v0.20.0...v0.21.0) (2026-09-28)


### Added

* **Propuestas de sub-agentes.** Con astromesh core v0.61.0 un sub-agente propone sobre la lista de quien lo llamó; la consola y el panel de corrida de Nexus muestran `vía <sub-agente>` en cada propuesta que no hizo el agente principal.

### Fixed

* **El test de snippets valida lo que Monaco inserta.** Validaba `TOOL_TEMPLATES`, una copia que ningún snippet usaba; ahora expande el `insertText` real de `tool-integration`, `tool-api` y `tool-mcp` y lo valida contra el schema. `TOOL_TEMPLATES` se eliminó.
* **ToolCard ya no anida un `<button>` dentro de otro** (HTML inválido, y el clic en quitar dependía de `stopPropagation`). El botón de quitar tiene `aria-label`.
* **Las filas del catálogo de integraciones no son botones mudos.** En el panel de catálogo de Nexus, que no selecciona, se dibujan como filas de solo lectura.

## [0.19.0] - 2026-08-06

### Added

- **Escritura en el panel Admin de operador** (`src/shells/nexus/panels/AdminPanel.tsx`): el panel dejó de ser solo lectura. Cubre los tres writes que el hub ya exponía y ninguna UI alcanzaba — `POST /api/v1/admin/tariffs`, `POST /api/v1/admin/plans` y `PUT /api/v1/admin/tenants/:id/plan` — de modo que crear una tarifa, cargar un plan o asignárselo a un tenant deja de requerir `curl` con el `X-Operator-Token` a mano. Los tres formularios viven en AdminPanel a propósito: el token de operador nunca se mezcla con el `X-API-Key`/JWT de tenant, así que ningún panel de tenant pasa a depender de su estado. Los cuerpos van en **snake_case** (los request structs del hub sí llevan json tags, al revés de las respuestas `Tariff`/`Plan`, que son PascalCase), `effective_from` se manda como RFC3339 UTC — el hub se niega a defaultearlo a ahora, porque un precio sin instante de inicio es uno del que ninguna factura se puede reproducir — y los seis límites del plan distinguen vacío (`null`, sin límite) de `0` (bloqueado). Nuevos helpers `toMicros`/`toLimit` en `nexusRunFormat.ts`, junto al `formatCredits` que invierten. El selector de tenant es texto libre y no un desplegable: `GET /api/v1/tenants` lista solo los tenants del usuario logueado, así que el hub no tiene ruta que se los enumere todos a un operador.

### Fixed

- **El 404 del panel Admin ya no confunde "no existe la fila" con "el hub no tiene admin"** (`src/shells/nexus/panels/nexusRunFormat.ts`): el mapeo de errores leía solo el status, así que un tenant id mal tipeado en el asignador de planes respondía «Admin no disponible en este hub» y mandaba al operador a revisar la configuración del hub en lugar del id. Los dos 404 se distinguen por el cuerpo, verificado contra el hub de dev: un grupo `/admin` sin registrar (hub sin `OperatorToken`) devuelve el texto plano `404 page not found` de gin, mientras que un handler registrado que no encuentra la fila devuelve un cuerpo JSON. `errText` pasó a ser `adminErrorMessage` y vive junto a `runErrorMessage`, su gemelo, con tests sobre ambos 404.

## [0.18.0] - 2026-07-29

### Added

- **Agent chaining and structured output in the YAML editor** (`src/schemas/agent.schema.json`, `src/components/editor/agent-snippets.ts`): the agent schema now knows `spec.chain` and `spec.output_schema` from astromesh core v0.38.1. Until now `spec` carried `additionalProperties: false`, so an agent declaring either section was **flagged as invalid in Monaco** — a valid manifest looked broken. The schema encodes the runtime's real constraints (`mode` limited to `sequential`/`parallel`, `on_complete` non-empty, `agent` required per link, `retry.backoff` limited to `fixed`/`exponential`), and the descriptions carry the rules that are easiest to get wrong: every matching rule fires (it is not an if/elif cascade), a link naming an agent that does not exist stops the runtime from starting, and older runtimes ignore both sections silently. New snippets for the `output_schema` and `chain` sections, plus a `chain` cursor context offering `chain-link` and `chain-link-default` entries.
- **Chain breakdown in agent run results** (`src/components/console/RunChainBreakdown.tsx`, `src/types/chain.ts`): a run against an agent that declares a chain now renders its links beneath the answer — agent, state and duration, nested links indented under their parent. **Links that did not fire are shown too**, greyed, with the reason (`condición falsa`, `ciclo`, `profundidad máxima`, `cortada antes`); the runtime reports them precisely so "why wasn't the email sent?" is answerable without opening the trace, and hiding them would throw that away. The summary line carries the chain's overall status and mode.

### Changed

- **Run contract gains `data` and `chain`** (`src/types/api.ts`, `src/hooks/useAgentRun.ts`, `src/stores/console.store.ts`): `AgentRunResponse` and `RunOutcome` carry the validated `spec.output_schema` object and the chain result. Both are optional and guarded by `isRunChain`, so a runtime older than v0.38.1 — which omits the fields entirely — degrades to "no chain" instead of throwing, the same contract `isRunUsage` already follows. The WebSocket path is unchanged: the `done` event carries neither field, so a streamed run shows no chain breakdown.

## [0.17.0] - 2026-07-27

### Added
- **Per-model usage breakdown in agent run results** (`src/components/console/RunUsageBreakdown.tsx`): a new `RunUsageBreakdown` component renders a UsoPanel-style table showing per-model consumption (provider / model / role / calls / tokens in-out / cost) from direct agent runs in `AgentConsole`. The breakdown collapses beneath the run's total token count when `usage.by_model` is present, surfacing provider and cost details from astromesh core v0.36.0. No credits or infra economics (hub-only features); the component visualizes only what the core's run response provides.

### Changed
- **Core run/WebSocket usage contract with per-model breakdown** (`src/services/agent-run-events.ts`, `src/types/api.ts`, `src/stores/console.store.ts`): `RunUsage` gained an optional `by_model: RunModelUsage[]` array carrying per-model/role/call metrics (tokens in/out, cost) from the runtime. `isRunUsage` predicate now validates and filters these rows; both `AgentRunResponse.usage` and `ChatMessage.usage` adopt the shared `RunUsage` type. Ecosystem and version references aligned to astromesh core **v0.36.0**. The `by_model` field is optional — runtimes older than v0.36.0 simply omit it without breaking the contract.
- **Vitest configuration cleanup** (`vitest.config.ts`): removed the dead `environmentMatchGlobs` option (ignored in Vitest v4) and added the `.test.tsx` include glob to improve test discovery.

## [0.16.0] - 2026-07-27

### Added
- **Operator "Admin" panel in the Nexus shell** (`src/shells/nexus/panels/AdminPanel.tsx`): a read-only view of the hub's current tariffs (`GET /api/v1/admin/tariffs`) and plans (`GET /api/v1/admin/plans`), authenticated with an operator token (`X-Operator-Token`) stored per-connection via `safeStorage`. The panel manages the token (set/clear) and renders each tariff's credits-per-1k and each plan's included credits + limits (`sin límite` for unset). Distinct from the tenant dual-auth; the group is hidden behind an unset-token empty state.

## [0.15.0] - 2026-07-27

### Added
- **"Uso" observability panel in the Nexus shell** (`src/shells/nexus/panels/UsoPanel.tsx`): a three-level view over the hub's observability endpoints — tenant overview (`GET /api/v1/usage`: month totals via a month selector + all-time + a per-agent ranking, soft-deleted agents flagged), per-agent drill (`/agents/:name/metrics` + recent invocations from `/agents/:name/logs`), and invocation detail (`/agents/:name/invocations/:id`: per-model breakdown + sub-invocations). Replaces the `MetricsPanel`/`LogsPanel`/`CostPanel` stubs and removes the vestigial `getAgentStatus` client method.

### Fixed
- **`UsoPanel` crash on invocation detail with no model rows or sub-invocations** (`src/shells/nexus/panels/UsoPanel.tsx`, `src/types/nexus.ts`): the hub's invocation-detail handler doesn't guard its Go nil slices, so `models`/`children` serialize as JSON `null` rather than `[]` for a leaf or errored invocation — the common case. `NexusInvocationDetail` now types both as nullable and `InvocationView` guards every read site. Also: a 501 from an older hub without `/usage` now shows the specced Spanish copy instead of the raw English marker, and switching the active tenant while drilled into an agent/invocation now resets the panel to the tenant overview instead of refetching stale state against the new tenant.

## [0.14.0] - 2026-07-27

### Added
- **Live streaming, cancellation, and persistent transcripts in the Nexus run panel** (`src/stores/nexus-run.store.ts`, `src/stores/nexus-run-persistence.ts`, `src/shells/nexus/panels/NexusRunPanel.tsx`, `electron/services/nexus.service.ts`): the run panel now streams a run over the hub's `GET /api/v1/agents/:name/run/stream` WebSocket (main-process `ws` client, since the handshake needs auth headers a browser `WebSocket` can't set), showing tool-call activity live and a **Stop** button that cancels the run in-flight (the hub records it `cancelled` and charges nothing). Transcripts persist per tenant in `localStorage` (terminal turns only, capped at 50 per agent) and reload on tenant activation. Falls back to the synchronous run when the hub lacks the stream route.

## [0.13.0] - 2026-07-26

### Added
- **Nexus agent run panel in Cortex** (`src/shells/nexus/panels/NexusRunPanel.tsx`, `src/shells/nexus/NexusShell.tsx`): `NexusShell`'s right panel now runs agents synchronously against the hub instead of mounting the runtime's `AgentConsole`. It lists the active tenant's agents (preselecting the one behind the active `nexus-yaml` editor tab), keeps an in-memory transcript per agent/session (⌘/Ctrl+Enter to send, "nueva sesión" to reset), and renders each result's answer plus its usage breakdown (tokens in/out, credits, per-model rows with `own` marker) via `formatUsage`. Friendly Spanish messages surface hub failures (draft agent without a published version, runtime down/timeout, rate limits). Built on the `runAgent` IPC chain, `nexus-client`, `nexusRunFormat` helpers, and the `useNexusRunStore` Zustand store from earlier tasks in this feature.
- **Compare two versions in the versions drawer** (`src/components/nexus/NexusVersionDiff.tsx`, `src/components/nexus/NexusVersionsPanel.tsx`): a "Comparar" mode lets you pick two versions (defaulting the second to the current one) and renders a read-only side-by-side Monaco diff of their specs (`DiffEditor` from `@monaco-editor/react`, YAML, minimap off), each side labelled `v{n} · sha {checksum}…` with an "(actual)" marker on the current version. `NexusVersionDiff` is lazy-loaded from the panel — same reasoning as `MonacoWrapper` in Task 2 — since it also imports `@monaco-editor/react`'s monaco/Vite-worker module graph, which would otherwise break the panel's Vitest unit tests.
- **Versions drawer in the agent editor** (`src/components/nexus/NexusVersionsPanel.tsx`, `src/components/nexus/specToYaml.ts`, `src/components/editor/NexusAgentYamlEditor.tsx`): a "Versiones" toggle opens a history drawer (number, date, author, checksum prefix, "actual" badge on the highest version) with per-version View (read-only YAML, rendered from the JSON spec via `specToYaml`/`js-yaml`, lazy-loaded `MonacoWrapper`) and Revert. Revert has no hub endpoint — it fetches the chosen version's spec, renders it back to YAML, and republishes it via the existing `updateAgent` PUT, appending a new current version; always gated behind `window.confirm`. The editor's agent-load effect is now a `reload()` callback so a successful revert refreshes the open editor to show the new current spec.
- **Agent version client methods** (`src/services/nexus-client.ts`, `electron/services/nexus.service.ts`, `electron/ipc/nexus.ts`, `electron/preload.ts`): `listAgentVersions(tenantId, name)` and `getAgentVersion(tenantId, name, number)` wired through the full service→IPC→preload→client chain (`GET /api/v1/agents/{name}/versions` and `/versions/{number}`), with the same `withIpcErrorMapping`/`NexusNotAvailableYet` handling as the other agent methods. New types `NexusVersionAuthor`, `NexusAgentVersionSummary`, `NexusAgentVersion`, `NexusAgentVersionList` in `src/types/nexus.ts`. Client plumbing only — no UI yet.
- **`type: client` tools (astromesh core v0.35.0).** The agent schema, the visual builder's
  tool picker (`ToolsInspector`), the Monaco snippets (`agent-snippets`) and the YAML helper
  now offer `client` alongside `builtin` and `agent` — the three types the runtime loads. A
  `client` tool is announced to the model but executed by the consumer, not the runtime; the
  call surfaces live through the run's `tool_call`/`tool_result` events (which the console
  already renders) and in the run's `steps`. In the visual builder it needs only a name and
  description — its `parameters` are authored in the YAML editor. This re-adds the type the
  v0.34.0 alignment held back while it was still on an unreleased astromesh branch; core
  v0.35.1 is otherwise a runtime-only provider fix (agent `model.timeout` reaching
  `openai_compat`), and Cortex's schema already accepts `timeout` in the model block.
- **Live agent runs in the console.** `AgentConsole` now streams a run over the runtime's
  WebSocket (`/v1/ws/agent/{name}`), which astromesh core v0.34.0 made live — it had been a
  stub that echoed the query back. In-flight the console shows each `tool_call` with its
  `tool_result` verdict and the model's per-iteration reasoning as transient narration; a
  Stop button closes the socket, which cancels the run server-side. Against a runtime older
  than v0.34.0 the stub's `response` event is detected and the run falls back to the
  blocking HTTP `POST /v1/agents/{name}/run`, so nothing breaks on an older runtime.
  A WebSocket run carries no `steps` or `trace` — v0.34.0's `done` event is
  `{answer, session_id, usage}` — so the per-message "View Trace" button appears only on
  HTTP runs. The Traces panel is unaffected.
- **`orbit upgrade` in the GCP panel** — diffs the Terraform templates re-rendered by the
  current Orbit package. Read-only: Cortex never passes `--apply`.
- **Orbit v0.3.0/v0.4.0 alignment in the deploy wizard.** The GCP wizard now configures
  `spec.storage` (RAG-documents bucket with versioning, Artifact Registry) and
  `spec.observability` (Cloud Monitoring dashboard, OpenTelemetry tracing sidecar with a
  configurable collector image), plus an **Export traces (OTLP)** toggle that injects
  `ASTROMESH_OTLP_ENABLED` when the tracing sidecar is off. The GCP panel gains read-only
  **Logs** (`orbit logs`) and **Status** (`orbit status`) actions.
- **Per-role model routing** (`src/schemas/agent.schema.json`, `src/types/api.ts`): agent `model` config now uses `model.default` plus named `model.roles.<name>`, each a `{ candidates: [...], strategy }` block. Candidates are ranked positionally and use `source` — `ollama` / `openai` / `openai_compat` / `azure_openai` / `litellm` (LiteLLM proxies 100+ cloud models). Roles are consumed by orchestration patterns (`reasoner`, `planner`/`worker`/`synthesizer`, `stage:<name>`, `supervisor`); undefined roles fall back to `default`. Mirrors astromesh's per-role `ModelRouter`
- **Per-role ModelInspector** (`src/components/visual-agent/inspectors/ModelInspector.tsx`): the visual builder edits the `default` role and named roles, each with a ranked candidate list (source incl. `litellm`, model, endpoint, API-key env, temperature) and a routing strategy; add/remove candidates and roles
- **RAG knowledge sync** (`src/schemas/rag.schema.json`, `src/components/visual-rag/`): a new `RAGPipeline` resource kind with a full visual builder (chunking / embeddings / vector store / reranking / retrieval), a YAML editor, a scaffold form, and a dedicated "RAG Pipelines" sidebar panel. Backed by astromesh's new `/v1/rag/pipelines` CRUD API (`src/services/api-client.ts`). Monaco validates RAGPipeline YAML via a dedicated schema scoped by the `.rag.yaml` filename suffix
- **Agent `spec.knowledge`** (`src/schemas/agent.schema.json`, `src/types/api.ts`): agents reference a RAGPipeline by name (`{ pipeline, top_k }`) instead of embedding an inline `rag` tool. The `KnowledgeInspector` edits this reference with a pipeline picker fed by the live pipeline list
- **Workflows + HITL** (`src/shells/runtime/panels/WorkflowsPanel.tsx`, `src/components/editor/WorkflowYamlEditor.tsx`, `src/services/api-client.ts`, `src/stores/workflow-runs.store.ts`): a dedicated "Workflows" sidebar panel that lists a runtime's workflows, runs them, tracks the runs it launches, and drives astromesh's human-in-the-loop approval loop — a pending-approval queue with inline approve/reject and optional comments. A "New Workflow" button opens a Monaco `*.workflow.yaml` editor (schema-validated) with Run and Register-blueprint actions. Backed by `/v1/workflows/*` client methods (list/get/run/runs/resume/approvals/approve/reject/register) and an in-memory run-tracking store.
- **Model `providerRef`** (`src/schemas/agent.schema.json`, `src/migration/model-config.ts`): a model candidate can reference a named astromesh ProviderConfig entry via `{ providerRef: <name> }` instead of an inline `source`/`model`; the runtime resolves endpoint/auth/contract from the registry and inline keys override. The visual builder's ModelInspector and the loader preserve it
- **Embedded terminal: Workflows + HITL** (`src/components/terminal/AstromeshTerminal.tsx`): the emulated `astromeshctl` REPL now covers `workflows list`/`workflows run`, `approvals`, `approve`, and `reject`, and fixes the previously-dead `trace <id>` command (listed in the registry but with no handler)
- **README**: documents Cortex's feature set (agent authoring with per-role model routing + `providerRef`, RAG pipelines, Workflows + HITL, the embedded `astromeshctl` terminal) and its place in the astromesh ecosystem, including that agents deployed via Leia, ADK, the CLI, or Forge surface in the Agents panel alongside those authored in Cortex

### Fixed
- **CI `npm ci` failed to resolve peer dependencies** — the repo runs `vite@8` but
  `electron-vite@5` only peers `vite@^5||^6||^7`, so `npm ci` errored with `ERESOLVE`
  and every develop CI job (Tests/Build/Typecheck) died at install. Bump
  `electron-vite` to `6.0.0-beta.1` (peers `vite@^6||^7||^8`); build/test verified
  locally. (Typecheck still surfaces pre-existing, unrelated type errors.)
- **`NexusAgentYamlEditor` still read the removed `NexusAgent.phase` field**
  (`src/components/editor/NexusAgentYamlEditor.tsx`): the live editor opened for
  `nexus-yaml` tabs kept `setPhase(agent.phase ?? null)` / `setPhase(result.phase ?? phase)`
  after `phase` was renamed to `status` across the feature (see the `NexusYamlPanel`
  migration above), so the status badge never rendered and the file failed the web
  typecheck. Renamed the local state to `status` and read `agent.status`/`result.status`,
  matching `NexusYamlPanel`.
- **`withIpcErrorMapping` never matched a real Electron IPC rejection**
  (`src/services/nexus-client.ts`): it re-instantiated `NexusNotAvailableYet` only when
  the error message `startsWith('Nexus endpoint not available yet: ')`, but
  `ipcRenderer.invoke()` rejects with that text prefixed by Electron's own framing
  (`Error invoking remote method '...': Error: Nexus endpoint not available yet: ...`),
  so the `startsWith` check never matched across the real IPC boundary and the 501
  mapping silently failed. Switched to `.includes(...)` (locating the marker before
  slicing the path), which still leaves ordinary hub errors like `Nexus API 409: ...`
  untouched. The test now simulates the prefixed IPC rejection instead of a bare message,
  so it actually exercises the boundary it claims to cover.
- **The agent YAML schema declared six tool types the runtime cannot load.**
  `spec.tools[].type` accepted `builtin`, `internal`, `mcp_stdio`, `mcp_sse`, `mcp_http`,
  `webhook`, `rag` and `agent`; the runtime's loader has branches for exactly two —
  `builtin` and `agent` — and silently discards every other type, so the tool never
  registers and never reaches the model. The editor was autocompleting and validating
  tools that would vanish at load time. The enum was narrowed to `builtin | agent` (and
  `client` was later added when astromesh v0.35.0 shipped it — see Added above). An existing
  YAML declaring `type: internal` now shows an error where it previously passed. The
  same narrowing now applies to every authoring surface that offered a tool type: the
  visual builder's tool picker (`ToolsInspector`, which also drops the dead
  `RagFields`/`McpFields`/`WebhookFields` editors), the Monaco snippets
  (`agent-snippets`), and the YAML helper panel — so the editor no longer
  autocompletes a type its own validator then rejects.

### Changed
- **Model config authored as new format only**: `model.primary` / `fallback` / `extra` / `routing` are removed from the authored schema (`provider` → `source`). Legacy configs loaded into the visual builder are **auto-migrated** to the per-role shape via `src/migration/model-config.ts` (`normalizeModelConfig`), which marks the config dirty so the upgrade can be saved
- **Knowledge migration** (`src/migration/knowledge-config.ts`): agents with a legacy inline `rag` tool are auto-migrated on load into `spec.knowledge` (marked dirty to save the upgrade); the embedding/chunking parameters move to the RAGPipeline resource
- **All editor surfaces emit the new format**: the new-agent scaffold (`NewAgentForm`), the Model YAML-helper card (`YamlHelper`), the Monaco completion snippets (`agent-snippets`), and the visual-builder node summary (`SatelliteNode`) now produce/display `model.default.candidates[].source` + `strategy` instead of the legacy `primary`/`routing` shape
- **Nexus shell de-K8s-ified** (`src/shells/nexus/NexusSidebar.tsx`, `NexusActivityBar.tsx`): the sidebar taxonomy drops the `Cluster`/`Workloads`/`Observability` K8s-operator framing in favor of `Tenants` · `Agentes` · `Accesos` · `Uso (próximamente)`, matching what the managed hub actually exposes. `DeploymentsPanel` is removed (there are no per-tenant workloads to browse); `NexusYamlPanel` now lives under `Agentes` and `AccessPanel`/`NexusSettingsPanel` under `Accesos`. The not-yet-real stubs (`UsersPanel`, `AuditPanel`, `LogsPanel`, `MetricsPanel`, `CostPanel`, `CatalogPanel`) keep their files but drop the placeholder `"Not supported by this Nexus version."` copy for text naming the real future endpoint (e.g. billing plane, per-agent status/logs/metrics, users/audit), and collapse into a `Más (próximamente)` group instead of a first-class tab. Also fixes residual compile errors left by the Task 1-5 type changes: `NexusShell` read a `nexusUrl` field that `NexusConnection` never had (it's `hubUrl`), and `NexusYamlPanel`/`TenantsPanel` still read the `.phase` field dropped from `NexusAgent`/`NexusTenant`

### Added

- **TofuManager**: new `electron/services/tofu-manager.ts` — downloads and manages the OpenTofu binary per-platform (win32/darwin/linux, x64/arm64)

### Changed

- **OrbitService**: `buildEnv()` now passes `TOFU_PATH` env var pointing to the bundled OpenTofu binary, so orbit's `TerraformRunner` finds it without PATH lookup

## [0.3.0] - 2026-04-06

### Added

- **GCP Deployments panel**: new sidebar panel in Runtime mode (Cloud icon) for managing Google Cloud Run deployments — configure credentials (gcloud CLI or Service Account key), view/redeploy/delete deployments, with Google blue (#4285F4) accent
- **GCP deploy target**: third option in Deploy split-button alongside Runtime and Nexus — badge shows "GCP" in blue when selected, persisted per-tab
- **DeployWizard for GCP**: 4-step guided flow (Auth → Configure → Plan → Deploy) that generates correct `OrbitConfig` schema (`apiVersion: astromesh/v1`, `kind: OrbitDeployment`), writes `orbit.yaml` to workspace, and streams `astromeshctl orbit plan/apply` output
- **Nexus Agent API (real)**: full IPC chain for agent CRUD — `POST/GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/agents` with `Content-Type: application/x-yaml` and `X-Tenant-ID` header for tenant-scoped operations
- **NexusYamlPanel (functional)**: lists deployed agents from Nexus API, click to open YAML editor for editing spec
- **NexusAgentYamlEditor (functional)**: fetch agent spec via `getAgent`, save via `updateAgent`, delete via `deleteAgent`, shows phase badge (Pending/Running/Error)
- **CLI auto-install**: Local Runtime install now includes `astromesh-cli` (step 5) and `astromesh-orbit[gcp]` (step 6) — 7 install steps total
- **GCP setup guide**: `docs/guides/gcp-setup.md` with both auth methods, IAM roles, troubleshooting; rendered in polished BrowserWindow with code blocks, sticky header, and GCP blue accent
- **Markdown renderer**: fenced code blocks (```lang) with language label header, CRLF normalization, unordered list support

### Changed

- **OrbitService**: resolves `astromeshctl` from local runtime venv path (`<userData>/local-runtime/venv/Scripts/`) instead of system PATH; platform-aware spawn (shell on Windows only)
- **Deploy split-button**: now dispatches to 3 targets — Runtime (cyan), Nexus (purple), GCP (blue)
- **TenantSelectorInline**: uses real tenant IDs from `nexusStore.tenants` (API-fetched) instead of manually typed workspace `tenantId`

### Fixed

- **Deploy to Nexus 403**: `handleDeployNexus` now fetches fresh tenant list from API to get real tenant IDs instead of relying on workspace connection's manually typed tenantId
- **Nexus agent operations 403**: all agent API methods (list/get/create/update/delete) pass `X-Tenant-ID` header propagated through IPC → preload → callers
- **DEP0190 warning**: OrbitService uses single-string command with shell on Windows (avoids passing args with `shell: true`)
- **Guide file not found**: renamed `gcp-deploy-setup.md` to `gcp-setup.md` matching `openGuide('gcp-setup')` call
- **Code blocks not rendering**: markdown renderer normalizes `\r\n` → `\n` before parsing fenced code blocks

## [0.2.0] - 2026-04-04

### Added

- **Workspace-centric architecture**: Projects are now folders with `.cortex/workspace.json` (versionable in git) holding multiple runtime + nexus connections, environments, and UI state. Embeddable in any git repo.
- **Welcome Page**: Fresh landing with "Open Folder" / "New Workspace" actions + recent workspaces list (persisted via `electron-store` under `cortex-app`)
- **WorkspaceService** (Electron): filesystem operations for `.cortex/workspace.json` + `local.json`, automatic `.gitignore` entry for `local.json`, file watching for external changes
- **WorkspaceShell**: TitleBar (workspace name + close) + ModeRouter + StatusBar. Debounced auto-save (500ms) + external-change reload
- **Dual-shell architecture**: `RuntimeShell` (open-source local dev) and `NexusShell` (cloud/Lens-like operator console) share a single `EditorArea` but have independent activity bars, sidebars, and bottom panels
- **ModeRouter**: `ui.mode` (`'runtime'` | `'nexus'`) mounts the appropriate shell; persisted to `workspace.json#ui.lastMode`
- **ModeSwitcher** (status bar): pill button with dropdown to toggle modes; `Ctrl+M` keyboard shortcut
- **ConnectionDropdown** (status bar): live-status beacon + mode-aware connection picker reading from workspace connections
- **EnvironmentDropdown** (status bar): environment selector pulling from `workspace.json#environments`
- **RuntimeShell**: Explorer · Agents · Runtime + Settings activity bar; Terminal · Activity · Output bottom tabs; reorganized panels under `src/shells/runtime/panels/`
- **RuntimeSettingsPanel**: CRUD for runtime connections (local/remote URL + type) scoped to active workspace
- **NexusShell**: 4-group activity bar (Cluster · Workloads · Observability · Catalog) + Settings, with tenant-drill-down sidebar (tenant selector persists the scope for Workloads/Observability/Catalog/Access)
- **NexusSidebar**: per-group subpanel routing (Tenants, Users & RBAC, Audit Log, Deployments, YAML Editor, Logs, Metrics, Cost, Catalog, API Keys, Connections)
- **NexusBottomPanel**: Events · Alerts · Remote Shell tabs (stubs pending Nexus streaming endpoints)
- **NexusLoginCard**: inline login form shown when the active Nexus connection has no authenticated session
- **TenantsPanel** (functional): lists tenants for the active Nexus connection
- **AccessPanel** (functional): API key management per tenant (create, revoke) with one-time-reveal of raw key
- **NexusSettingsPanel** (functional): CRUD for Nexus connections (name + URL + tenantId) scoped to active workspace
- **8 Nexus panel stubs**: Users, Audit, Deployments, NexusYaml, Logs, Metrics, Cost, Catalog — each displaying "Not supported by this Nexus version" until the corresponding endpoint ships
- **NexusAgentYamlEditor**: edit-only YAML editor for deployed Nexus agents; `GET/PUT /api/v1/tenants/:id/agents/:name` endpoints stubbed pending Nexus implementation
- **Deploy split-button** in `AgentYamlEditor`: primary action deploys to persisted target; dropdown lets you switch between Runtime (cyan) or any Nexus connection (magenta). Target is persisted per-tab in `editor.store` and shown as an inline badge next to Rocket icon
- **Mode-aware editor tabs**: tabs carry `mode: 'runtime' | 'nexus' | 'shared'` (derived from tab type); tabs incompatible with active mode render disabled with tooltip "Open in <mode> mode"
- **Legacy settings migration**: on first launch after upgrade, detects `astromesh-settings` localStorage and prompts the user to create a workspace with migrated connections (`local`/`remote` → runtime, `nexus` → nexus)
- **Workspace IPC surface**: `workspace:open/create/save/save-local/pick-folder/watch/unwatch/read-file/write-file/list-files` + recent-workspaces CRUD
- **Nexus tenant normalization**: service now accepts both camelCase and snake_case API responses (`displayName`/`display_name`, `crName`/`cr_name`, `id`/`ID`/`tenantId`, etc.) so Cortex works against Nexus deployments that don't match the spec exactly
- **Design spec**: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-04-workspace-dual-layout-design.md` — workspace entity, shell architecture, mode switching, migration
- **Implementation plan**: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-04-workspace-dual-layout.md` — 28 tasks across 9 phases with full code + tests

### Changed

- **StatusBar**: now integrates ModeSwitcher + ConnectionDropdown + EnvironmentDropdown; runtime metrics (`v{version}`, agents count, mode) render only in Runtime mode; beacon color reflects *actual liveness* (runtime `status === 'running'` or Nexus session active) — not just "profile selected"
- **`useClient` hook**: reads active runtime connection from `workspace.store` instead of deleted `settings.store`; returns `null` when `ui.mode !== 'runtime'` (so runtime hooks idle in Nexus mode instead of hitting the wrong URL)
- **App routing**: `App.tsx` shows `WelcomePage` when no workspace is open, `WorkspaceShell` when `workspace.store.path` is set
- **Runtime activity bar**: simplified to Explorer · Agents · Runtime + Settings (Visual Builder removed — canvas is already a tab type opened from Agents panel)
- **`ui.store`**: gains `mode` field; `activeActivity` split into `runtimeActivity` + `nexusActivity` so each shell has independent sidebar state
- **`editor.store.EditorTab`**: gains `mode` field; `openTab()` auto-derives mode from tab type
- **Keyboard shortcuts**: `Ctrl+M` toggles mode (new); `Ctrl+S`, `Ctrl+B`, `Ctrl+J`, `Ctrl+F4`, `Ctrl+Shift+P` wired in `WorkspaceShell` (previously in deleted `IDEShell`)

### Fixed

- **Tenant names not rendering** in TenantSelector: service normalizes API responses that used snake_case (`display_name`) or different key casings, matching the payload shape regardless of Nexus version
- **Local Runtime appearing as "connected" when stopped**: StatusBar beacon now reflects actual connection health per profile type (runtime: `status === 'running'`, nexus: `isConnected`)
- **"Failed to fetch" in Explorer when connected via Nexus**: runtime-specific hooks (`useAgents`, `useTemplates`, etc.) idle in Nexus mode instead of hitting the Nexus URL with `/v1/*` paths
- **Test button not opening RightPanel**: `RightPanel` was missing from the new `RuntimeShell`/`NexusShell` layouts after the shell split — restored in both
- **Keyboard shortcuts broken after shell split**: `Ctrl+S`, `Ctrl+B`, `Ctrl+J`, `Ctrl+F4`, `Ctrl+Shift+P` were wired only in the deleted `IDEShell` — rewired in `WorkspaceShell`
- **Nexus session not restored** on app launch: `restoreSession()` + `onSessionExpired` listener restored in `WorkspaceShell`

### Removed

- **Legacy `settings.store`**: replaced by `workspace.store`; auto-migration on first launch after upgrade
- **`components/settings/` directory**: `SettingsPanel`, `ProfileCard`, `ConnectionForm`, `GcpCredentialsForm` replaced by per-shell settings panels (`RuntimeSettingsPanel`, `NexusSettingsPanel`)
- **Single-shell components**: `IDEShell.tsx`, `Sidebar.tsx`, `ActivityBar.tsx`, `BottomPanel.tsx` replaced by shell-specific variants under `src/shells/runtime/` + `src/shells/nexus/`
- **Visual Builder activity item** (Runtime mode): redundant with `visual-agent` editor tabs opened from Agents panel

### Migration notes for developers

- **State location**: profiles moved from `settings.store.profiles` to `workspace.store.config.connections.runtime[]` + `workspace.store.config.connections.nexus[]`. Active connection per mode: `activeRuntimeId` / `activeNexusId`.
- **API hook consumers**: anything calling `useClient()` now returns `null` in Nexus mode — guard accordingly (`if (!client) return`)
- **Electron IPC**: new `window.electronAPI.workspace.*` surface exposes workspace fs operations; `window.electronAPI.workspace.listRecent()` replaces any `astromesh-settings`-based recents
- **New directory layout**: runtime UI lives under `src/shells/runtime/`, Nexus UI under `src/shells/nexus/`, workspace shell under `src/components/workspace/`, status bar sub-components under `src/components/statusbar/`
- **Tab types**: if you add a new editor tab type, include it in the runtime/nexus arrays in `src/stores/editor.store.ts#deriveMode()` so mode-gating works
- **Pending Nexus endpoints** (wired with TODO stubs): `GET/PUT /api/v1/tenants/:id/agents/:name`, `POST /api/v1/tenants/:id/agents/:name/deploy`, list-deployed-agents, logs streaming, metrics, events, alerts, audit, users, cost

### Earlier in this release cycle — Nexus Cloud Integration

- **Nexus Cloud Integration**: Direct connection to Astromesh Nexus (Kubernetes control plane) for cloud agent management
- **NexusService**: Electron main-process HTTP client with encrypted token storage (safeStorage), automatic JWT refresh on 401, and session management
- **Nexus IPC Bridge**: Full preload bridge (`window.electronAPI.nexus.*`) for auth, tenant, and API key operations
- **NexusClient**: Renderer-side service wrapping IPC calls with typed responses
- **Nexus Zustand Store**: Reactive state for session (user, tenants, active tenant, keys) with login/register/logout/restoreSession actions
- **NexusLogin Component**: Login/Register form with Nexus URL configuration, email/password auth, error display, and mode toggle
- **TenantSelector Component**: Tenant list with active indicator, inline create form, and delete action
- **NexusStatusBadge**: Status bar indicator showing Nexus connection state and active tenant
- **Nexus Sidebar Panel**: Activity bar entry (Cloud icon) with conditional rendering — login form when disconnected, tenant manager when connected
- **Session Restore**: Automatic session restoration on app startup with session-expired listener for graceful logout
- **Nexus Connection Profile**: New `'nexus'` connection type in settings store alongside `'local'` and `'remote'`
- **CI/CD Workflows**: GitHub Actions for build (`electron-vite build`), tests (`vitest`), and typecheck (`tsc --noEmit`)
- **README**: Project overview with architecture diagram, quick start, and tech stack table

### Previously in Unreleased

- **Service Account Guide**: "How to create a Service Account?" button opens a dedicated Electron window with step-by-step GCP setup instructions rendered from markdown
- **Command Palette**: Ctrl+Shift+P with fuzzy search, keyboard navigation, and grouped commands
- **Session Stats**: Accumulated tokens (input/output) and total time displayed in console footer
- **Config Directory Picker**: Native folder dialog pre-configured to current path for local runtime
- **Port Input**: Validated input that commits on blur/Enter instead of every keystroke

### Fixed

- **GCP Service Account toggle not persisting**: Clicking "Service Account" reverted to "gcloud CLI" because `authMethod` was derived from `keyFilePath` existence instead of being stored; now persisted in settings store
- **Service Account key verification always failing**: `readServiceAccountKey` returned `{ email, projectId }` but renderer expected `{ valid, projectId, clientEmail }`; aligned return types across Electron service, IPC, and components
- **GCP credentials not passed to deploy subprocess**: `astromeshctl orbit plan/apply` spawned without `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` env var; now injected when a service account key file is configured
- **HMR full reload on save/deploy**: Vite file watcher was detecting changes in `config/agents/` (where runtime stores YAML files), causing full app reload and navigation reset to Explorer. Excluded `config/` from watcher
- **Status badge showing "draft" for deployed agents**: Editors now fetch status from agent list API on mount instead of reading non-existent `metadata.labels.status` from YAML config
- **Duplicate API calls on invalidation**: `useAgents()` removed from editor components to prevent cascade re-renders; editors manage status locally from API responses
- **Background refetch flashing loader**: `useApiQuery` no longer sets `loading: true` on refetches when data already exists
- **Resize handle double border**: Removed duplicate `borderRight`/`borderLeft`/`borderTop` from panels; ResizeHandle now serves as the sole border between panels
- **Monaco worker errors**: Removed unnecessary JsonWorker, added ES worker format config

### Changed

- **Resize handles**: Now show a persistent subtle border line (`var(--am-border)`) at rest, cyan on hover, bright cyan with glow when dragging
- **Editor toolbar layout**: Right zone reorganized as `[toast] → [status badge] → [Visual/YAML] → [|] → [delete]` with vertical separator isolating delete
- **Action toasts**: Redesigned as pill-shaped badges with glow effect and `toast-in` animation
- **Tab dirty indicator**: Cyan filled dot replaces X icon; close confirmation dialog on dirty tabs
- **Status badge**: Uppercase tracking with border, consistent across YAML and Visual editors

## [0.1.0] - 2026-04-01

### Added

- **IDE Shell**: Electron + React desktop application with resizable panels (sidebar, editor, bottom panel, right panel)
- **Agent YAML Editor**: Monaco-based editor with YAML schema validation, autocomplete, contextual snippets, and section navigator (YamlHelper)
- **Visual Agent Builder**: Drag-and-drop agent editor with ReactFlow canvas, block palette, inspector panel, and bidirectional YAML sync
- **New Agent Form**: Scaffolding wizard to create agents from scratch with provider/model selection
- **Agent Console**: Interactive chat panel for testing agents against a running runtime
- **Local Runtime Manager**: One-click install of Astromesh runtime via `uv`, with Python 3.12 venv creation, health polling, orphan process detection, and auto-start
- **Runtime Controls**: UI for start/stop/restart/update/uninstall, port configuration, config directory picker, and live log streaming
- **Health Indicator**: Real-time latency and uptime display for running runtimes
- **Settings Panel**: Connection profiles with URL, API key, and type selection; GCP credentials via gcloud or service account
- **GCP Deploy Wizard**: Multi-step deployment to Cloud Run with auth, config, plan review, and apply stages
- **Orbit Electron Service**: IPC bridge for GCP CLI operations (gcloud, orbit) with log streaming
- **Activity Bar**: VS Code-style sidebar navigation with Explorer, Agents, Templates, Tools, and Settings sections
- **Tab System**: Multi-tab editor with dirty indicator (cyan dot), close confirmation for unsaved changes, and Ctrl+F4 shortcut
- **Keyboard Shortcuts**: Ctrl+S (save), Ctrl+B (toggle sidebar), Ctrl+J (toggle bottom panel), Ctrl+F4 (close tab)
- **Resize Handles**: 8px hit-zone for comfortable resizing with 1px visual line and hover/active states
- **Status Badges**: Live agent status (deployed/draft/paused) sourced from API in both YAML and Visual editors
- **Action Toasts**: Animated pill-shaped feedback for Save/Deploy/Pause operations with glow effect
- **Terminal Panel**: Integrated terminal via xterm.js in the bottom panel
- **API Client**: REST client for Astromesh runtime with agent CRUD, deploy/pause, templates, tools, and traces
- **Theme System**: CSS custom properties with dark theme, cyan accent palette, and consistent design tokens

### Fixed

- Runtime install stuck at "Creating environment" — added `--python 3.12` to `uv venv` to prevent wrong Python version discovery
- `uv venv --clear` failing with "Acceso denegado" on Windows — now removes venv manually before creating, kills orphaned processes on the configured port
- Uninstall failing with EBUSY on `uvicorn.exe` — kills orphaned processes before attempting directory removal
- Status badge showing "unknown" instead of "draft" for new agents
- Resize handle too thin (1px) to grab — expanded hit-zone to 8px with centered visual line

### Changed

- Editor store now supports `registerSaveHandler` / `saveActiveTab` for global Ctrl+S across all editor types
- Delete button separated from action group with a vertical divider in both editor toolbars
